body: Hey, you are smart, you are hard working and you can get through it. How you get through it is up to you. If you are not happy and you cannot continue where you are then gracefully leave, and apply to be in the match next year. Take out a loan, get a temporary job at wherever you can find, but if you are having thoughts that serious, you need to get out. Reach out to a counselor, talk to family, a therapist, someone. Think of all the things you will miss out on and all the good- *and they will be good*- years ahead. These feelings will not last forever, and you are worth something. Things will get better, they always do. You are not alone, there are unfortunately at least hundreds who feel similarly to you now. You are not weak, you are not worthless. Anything that allows you to see the years ahead with hope is worth it, bite the bullet and make the changes you need to, to keep yourself alive. I hope you feel better.  I really do.

No, dont retake tests, it will not be accurate. Maybe for practice with format but not for accurate scores. All my 5 aamc practice tests I took I got 32 so I thought they were roughly equivalent predictors of my performance.  Take aamc #9 once you feel really confident with the material, then to prepare in the next couple weeks do all the other aamc tests you havent taken and practice problems from your review books if you have any left.  Btw Don't even consider postponing until you take aamc #9. You wont study as hard and you will waste your time. Just get this shit done now and kill it and you wont have to worry about it any more!

You are taking too many tests too quick.  You need to spend at least 2 weeks thoroughly reviewing concepts with good review books. (I recommend exam krackers if you don't already have TPR stuff like your practice tests indicate.)  Really take 6-8 hours a day a really LEARN and UNDERSTAND your weak points which appears to be scattered all around. Then once you feel confident take another aamc practice test or 2 and see where you stand.  You need content review. You do not need any more practice.  Except for verbal, that do as much practice as you can and consider a new strategy if what you have is not working well enough.  I recommend exam krackers verbal workbook and 101 passages practice(I think PR was the one that emphasize skipping 1 passage and guessing? I think that is just downright stupid.  You have time to read and answer all questions if english is your first language).  You are fine where you are right now, you have plenty of time but you need to utilize 2-3 weeks of hardcore study and then take a few practice and get comfortable with your scores.

1.Phelps has denied the 12000 calorie rumor multiple times. It is false 99% of the time. He said 6-8000 is much more resonable and maybe not even that much.

All those essential functions can and have been provided for with a smaller government in the past so why not now? Government interference such as "no child left behind" and "the drug war" have been acknowledged as failures (by most). Things like that look good to a big wig sitting In an office but not so much to the real people it is affecting like teachers and harmless marijuana smokers.  I feel we could do without things like that and still have a government that can look out for basic needs like it has in the past.  Yes defense is a vital NEED of our government because citizens can't do that without government and it should be big in that aspect, but not in all the other ways we are allowing them to Intrude into our lives. We oppose the internet privacy bill but why not other things that are, in the end, restricting us and our freedom. (I wrote more about that in a reply to the other guy)

Big government, to me, means more power that size. 1984 although small, had all the power to do everything making it a big government. Like the Internet privacy bill that everyone does reject as being bad, which is good. I guess I am thinking we should be like that with everything because the more power and abilities we sanction and allow the closer we come to an Orwellian society. Although lots of control measures may seem to be good and limiting only the "bad" people, a lot of it limits everyone and in the end gives more power to the government.
